title: FORUM DATA INNOVATION AND SCIENCE CLUSTER DISC
description: FORUM, ESA's 9th Earth Explorer mission, is currently planned for launch in Q4 2028, with a nominal mission lifetime of five years.The mission will provide interferometric measurements across the 6.25-100 m spectral range, including the Far Infrared (FIR, approximately 15-100 m), which accounts for approximately 50% of the Earth's outgoing longwave radiation and up to 60% in polar regions.By addressing this critical observational gap, FORUM will provide unique measurements to advance our understanding of the Earth's energy budget and enable detailed investigations of the role and interactions of essential climate variables.The purpose of this procurement is to establish the FORUM Data Innovation and Science Cluster (DISC). The DISC concept has been successfully implemented byESA for previous Earth Explorer missions and is based on a consortium bringing together the scientific and technical expertise required to support the specific objectives and data quality needs of the mission.The FORUM DISC consortium will support ESA's Earth Observation Programmes - Sensor Performance, Products and Algorithms Section (EOP-GMQ) in the generation, calibration and validation (Cal/Val), monitoring, and quality control (QC) of FORUM mission products, as well as in their maintenance and evolution throughout the mission lifetime.The FORUM DISC contract will be structured into three main phases:Pre-launch phase: covering primarily the development, integration, verification and preparation for operational use of the FORUM processors, together with the associated quality monitoring and calibration/validation tools and procedures.Commissioning phase: covering the in-orbit commissioning activities, including the operation and validation of the implemented processors, tools and procedures, as well as the initial calibration and validation of FORUM mission products.Operations and mission exploitation phase: covering the nominal Cal/Val and quality monitoring activities during Phase E2 of the mission, together with the maintenance and evolution of algorithms, products, and processors.

title: LEAD-FREE ELECTRICAL ASSEMBLY TECHNOLOGY FOR HIGH RELIABILITY ELECTRICAL CONNECTIONS
description: Objective Development of lead-free solder processes and surface finishes for printed circuit board (PCB) assemblies enabling the future certification of European electronic assembly lines.DescriptionThe development of lead-free technology is important for theEuropean electronic manufacturers to maintain a competitiveposition in the global space market and enabling the use of stateof-the-art components developed for lead-free processesSignificant expertise with leadfree materials and processes has been developed in the commercial and automotive sectors. However, this knowledge does not sufficiently address the stringent reliability requirements,harsh environmental conditions, and long mission durations that characterise space applications.As highlighted in the ESCC LeadFree Transition Roadmap, a dedicated and sustained investmentestimated at 11 million is required over the next decade to mature leadfree technologiesfor reliable use in the European space sector. Some of the activities identified in the roadmap are currently underwayfor example, ESA activity (5C411 Pb-free assembly technologies for telecom satellites equipment) focused on the preliminary selection of candidate alloys and the LETTERS initiative funded by the European Union. The knowledge gained so far highlights the fundamental differences between leadfree solder alloys and the tinlead alloys currently in use. These differences have direct implications for mechanical behaviour, microstructural stability, and long-term reliability, and they reinforce the need for a deeper understanding of the fundamental properties and failure mechanisms associated with leadfree systems.This proposed activity directly supports the LeadFree Transition Roadmap updated in 2024. It builds on the knowledge generated by completed work and targets critical knowledge gaps that remain unaddressed by earlier initiatives. The outcomes of this activity will provide essential inputs for the definition of robust,evidence-based requirements and will form the technicalfoundation for future verification and approval of space grade assembly processes.The activity is structured into two main work packages. The first work package focuses on developing the fundamental knowledge required to understand the behaviour of leadfree technologies, including material interactions, microstructural evolution, andreliability critical mechanisms. The second work package is dedicated to the development and optimisation of assembly processes, as well as the creation and validation of supporting toolssuch as testing methodologies and modelling techniquesthat will enable the design and manufacturing ofreliable space qualified equipment. Together, these work-packages address capability gaps that arecommon across the entire European space electronics supply chain. The outcome of this activity will provide the base for the verification and certification flow of European assembly lines using Lead-free technologies for space use.Work package 1: Lead-free finishes and alloys characterizationThis work package focuses on the fundamental characterization of the most promising leadfree solder alloys and PCB finishes for high reliability space applications. This work requires strong involvement from academic partners to support advanced materials analysis. The alloys to be characterised include Innolot,a low melting point alloy, and SAC305 as a benchmark. PCB finishes will cover current leadfree industry options such as ENIG and future Ni free alternatives.This work package encompasses the following tasks:- Selection of candidate alloys and finishes based onliterature, ongoing activities, and industry needs.- Characterization of solder alloys (mechanical properties,creep, nano-indentation, metallurgical analysis), with focus onmicrostructure evolution during aging.- Study of intermetallic compound formation with differentfinishes and their evolution underextended aging.- Reliability testing on simple assemblies (e.g., resistors,capacitors) to correlate test conditions, microstructurechanges, and failure mechanisms.- Evaluation of tin whisker growth propensity for the selected alloys and assemblies.Key output: Knowledge of the fundamental properties of the materials allowing to identify parameters and mechanisms affecting the reliability of simple solder connection. Definition of standard accelerated test conditions that can be applied to the different alloys for the assessment of the reliability of assemblies.Data for development of modelling tools.Work package 2: Assembly Process Development,Reliability Assessment, and ModellingWork package 2 evaluates the impact of the selected leadfree alloys on assembly processes, equipment, ancillary materials,and PCB substrates. It also includes reliability testing of complex assemblies and the development of modelling tools. Involvingmultiple assembly houses and PCB manufacturers ensures representative and industry relevant data.This work package encompasses the following tasks:- Define a comprehensive test matrix covering SMT/THTcomponents, PCB materials and finishes, solder alloys,assembly processes, and conformal coating options.- Specify environmental test conditions (vibration, shock,thermal cycling), including dedicated thermal cycling only samples.- Design and manufacture electrically monitored testvehicles.- Develop and refine modelling tools for lead-free assemblyreliability.- Assess the impact of soldering and repair conditions onPCB materials and sensitive components.- Evaluate ancillary materials (fluxes, cleaning agents) and define baseline process requirements.- Use automated inspection to generate data for modelling and workmanship guidance.- Perform reliability testing to failure and analyse failuremechanisms.- Validate modelling tools against experimental results.- Draft an ECSS workmanship and certification standard for lead-free soldering.Key output: identification and full characterization of lead-free solder alloy(s) suitable for high reliability space application,development of best practices, modelling tools, test protocols and data in the form of draft ECSS soldering and workmanship standard for lead-free technology.

title: HE-ESA-026 STAGE 1 - SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND TEST BEACON FOR GOVERNMENTAL SAR
description: HE-ESA-026 Stage 1 - System architecture and test beacon for Governmental SAR- The objective of this activity is to prepare a future Search And Rescue service for governmental users with the testing of the key functions  of the end to end system, based on the development and use of a test beacon. The activity will consolidate and demonstrate the required test beacon technologies verifying endto end system performance.This activity belongs to Galileo/EGNOS Upstream RD which is part of the space component of Horizon Europe, under which, in line with the signed FFPA and relevant Contribution Agreement, ESA is delegated by the European Commission to manage this activity. ESA adapted procurement rules will apply as per the ITT to be published (open Competition in 2 stages). ESA reserves the right to place one parallel Contract subject to weighted quality of the proposal of at least 60 points, budget availabilityand related programmatic decision.
